summary: A low-risk, rules-clean regrid of a 2.8/4.0 us epilogue (full verify_16/32 only) whose best case is about 0.2% on the headline, so it can only be read from the _paired_norm_gate_kernel profile row; run it only if full-verify-cuda-streamk-splitkv (running now, which removes this kernel) does not land first.
justification: Mechanism: on master, _paired_norm_gate_kernel runs only on the paired path (window == 0, batch > 1, not splitkv), which means full verify_16 and verify_32 only. The decode shapes went to the CUDA split-KV path, and batch 1 is unpaired. Profile de486093311d4bb9 measures it at 2.8 us (verify_16, 1.6% of 169 us) and 4.0 us (verify_32, 1.3% of 300.6 us). It moves about 1.5 MB at verify_32 (1 MB of the 128-wide FA3 output, of which only half is read, plus 0.25 MB of gate and 0.25 MB written), which is about 0.3 us at 4.8 TB/s. So it sits 10x or more above its bandwidth floor and is bound by latency and per-CTA overhead (4096 one-warp CTAs, each doing a serial load -> reduce -> gate load -> store chain on 128 B rows), not by bandwidth. Moving to 256 four-warp programs, each loading a [16,64] tile (8 elements per thread, with the attn and gate loads independent so both can be in flight), is a plausible way to get to about 1.5 us. Expected directions match the routing: faster at full verify_16/32, flat elsewhere, because no other shape runs this kernel. Magnitude against TASK weights: verify_32 load = 46*28.7 + 16*300.8 = about 6130 us, and saving 16*2.5 us is about -0.65%. verify_16 load is about 3640 us, and saving 16*1.3 us is about -0.6%. The geomean over 6 loads is about +0.2%, far inside the +-1.5% CI. The weakest link is the claim that CTA count is the bottleneck. With 4096 one-warp CTAs, every CTA is resident in one wave (132 SMs x 32 CTAs), so the 4 us may mostly be kernel-launch/ramp latency plus the dependent-load chain, which the regrid does not remove. The sibling precedent preattention-group-tiled-programs (the same one-warp -> tiled regrid on _pre_attention_kernel) came out neutral within CI, and its full verify rows were flat. The realistic win is 1-2 us on the kernel row, possibly less. There is also no PDL on this Triton launch, so the gap between FA3 and the epilogue stays either way.
confounders: fa3-hdim128-head-pairing: created the [tokens,16,128] paired output this kernel reads, including the half = (h // G) % 2 indexing; without pairing the kernel does not exist and the unpaired path uses sglang rms_norm_gate. This is the base, not a confounder of the measured delta.
paired-heads-launch-cleanup: introduced _paired_norm_gate_kernel itself; the hypothesis edits only its grid and tiling, so the measured delta is attributable to the change.
paired-heads-launch-cleanup-ab-tune-batch-gate: limits pairing to batch > 1, which is why verify_1 is unaffected. This is consistent with the expected 'flat' rows.

full-decode-cuda-gather-splitkv: moved full decode_16/32 off the paired path, so the kernel now runs only at verify_16/32. This shrinks the hypothesis's reach to 2 of 12 shapes but does not confound the measurement.

Not landed but decisive: full-verify-cuda-streamk-splitkv (running) replaces the paired FA3 path and this epilogue at full verify_16/32. If it lands, this hypothesis is moot. If this one is measured first, its result does not carry over.
interference: No companion is warranted. The change has no sub-changes to isolate: it is one regrid with identical arithmetic. No landed hypothesis could plausibly flip its sign through interaction, because the kernel reads FA3's output and the gate, and FA3 and the pre-attention kernel are unchanged. Neither an ab-revert nor an ab-tune would make the headline readable, because the effect (about 0.2% geomean) is below the noise floor whatever runs next to it. The interpretable readout is the _paired_norm_gate_kernel row in the profile at verify_16/32 (base 2.8/4.0 us), together with the full verify_16/32 shape times. Judge it as a gain if the kernel row drops by at least 1 us and no shape regresses outside CI. Sequencing matters more than companions: hold dispatch until full-verify-cuda-streamk-splitkv is harvested, and drop this hypothesis if that one lands.
open_questions: Did full-verify-cuda-streamk-splitkv land? If it did, this kernel no longer runs on any scored shape and the hypothesis should be retired, not run.

Is the 4.0 us kernel time launch/ramp-bound (in which case a regrid gains little and PDL or folding the epilogue into FA3's combine, as fused-full-combine-normgate proposes, is the real lever) or per-CTA-overhead-bound (in which case the regrid helps)? An nsys/ncu look at achieved occupancy and the CTA count per SM would settle it before spending a check.

Correctness detail for the implementer: the per-row column offset depends on the row (half = (h // G) % 2 varies with h), so the [16,64] load needs a 2-D pointer block with a per-row offset, not a single base plus arange. The tl.sum over axis 1 must stay in fp32.
